opening_hook: December 2023. The war room at Zomato's Gurugram headquarters was quieter than usual. Deepinder Goyal sat across from his logistics team, staring at a slide that told an uncomfortable story: Blinkit's dark stores in Tier 2 cities — Indore, Bhopal, Jaipur, Lucknow — were burning through ₹180 crore a quarter with no path to profitability in sight. Outside, the temperature had dropped to 8°C. Inside the boardroom, the heat was of a different kind. The question on the table was not whether to act, but how fast — and how much collateral damage was acceptable. [Pg. 4]Q-commerce unit economics in non-metro markets remained deeply negative in H2 FY24, with average order values 34% below the metro baseline. — Zomato Q3 FY24 Investor Presentation, p. 4
company_background: Zomato Limited, founded in 2008 by Deepinder Goyal and Pankaj Chaddah as a restaurant menu aggregator, had evolved over fifteen years into one of India's most complex and ambitious technology companies. Listed on the BSE and NSE in July 2021 in a landmark ₹9,375 crore IPO — India's largest tech IPO at the time — Zomato had by 2023 expanded far beyond food delivery into logistics infrastructure, quick commerce, dining-out services, and B2B supply chain. [Pg. 7]Zomato was incorporated in 2008. The Company completed its IPO in July 2021, raising ₹9,375 crore at a valuation of approximately $5.4 billion. — Zomato Annual Report FY23, p. 7 Its acquisition of Blinkit (formerly Grofers) in 2022 for ₹4,447 crore in an all-stock deal was the boldest bet in that expansion — a wager that instant grocery delivery, executed through a dense network of 'dark stores' (micro-warehouses), would become as large as restaurant food delivery within five years. By Q2 FY24, Zomato employed over 5,900 full-time staff and supported a network of 3.5 lakh delivery partners across 500+ cities.
industry___competitive_context: The Indian quick commerce market, estimated at $3.3 billion in GMV in 2023 by RedSeer Consulting, was growing at 77% CAGR — but it was also brutally competitive and geographically uneven. The model, pioneered globally by Gorillas and Getir in Europe and domestically refined by Swiggy Instamart and Zepto, depends on three interlocking conditions: sufficiently dense urban populations to generate order frequency, customers with high basket values and low price sensitivity, and proximity of dark stores to maximize delivery speed. [Pg. 12]The top 8 metro and Tier 1 markets account for 81% of India's quick commerce GMV. — IBEF Quick Commerce Report, India, 2023, p. 12 In metro markets — Mumbai, Delhi-NCR, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Chennai, Pune — all three conditions held. In Tier 2 cities, none of them reliably did. Average order values in Tier 2 cities hovered at ₹280–320, compared to ₹480–540 in metro markets. Order frequency per dark store was 40–60 daily, against the breakeven threshold of 120–150. Zepto had already quietly withdrawn from six Tier 2 cities by mid-2023.
the_challenge: Blinkit's Tier 2 expansion had been aggressive. Between Q4 FY23 and Q2 FY24, the network grew from 28 dark stores in non-metro markets to 67 — a strategy built on the assumption that early geographic presence would create durable market share before competition arrived. That assumption proved incorrect on three dimensions. First, demand density was insufficient: Tier 2 customers demonstrated strong price sensitivity and preferred hyperlocal kirana stores for grocery top-ups. Second, supply chain economics were adverse: unlike metros where a single supplier could service 15–20 dark stores, Tier 2 geographies required individual procurement relationships, raising COGS by 18–22%. Third, delivery partner retention was structurally difficult — average partner tenure in Tier 2 was 11 weeks, versus 34 weeks in metros. [Pg. 18]Delivery partner retention rates in non-metro markets were 3.1x lower than metro markets in Q2 FY24. — Zomato Q2 FY24 Investor Letter, p. 18 Each Blinkit order in Tier 2 cities cost ₹94 more to fulfil than a comparable metro order, while generating ₹62 less in contribution margin.
intervention: In January 2024, Zomato announced the consolidation of Blinkit's dark store footprint — closing 48 of its 67 Tier 2 city stores over a 90-day transition window, retaining only 19 locations in cities that showed viable order economics (Jaipur, Chandigarh, Kochi). Capital freed from Tier 2 operations — approximately ₹220 crore in annualized fixed costs — was redeployed into three metro-focused initiatives: (1) accelerating dark store count in Bengaluru and Delhi-NCR from 38 to 62 stores; (2) investing in Blinkit's proprietary inventory management system, 'Nucleus', which reduced holding costs by 14% through AI-driven demand forecasting; and (3) launching Blinkit Ads — an in-app sponsored placement product for FMCG brands — which reached ₹40 crore ARR within two quarters. [Pg. 24]The Blinkit Ads platform reached annualised revenue of ₹40 crore by Q1 FY25, contributing a high-margin revenue stream with zero incremental delivery cost. — Zomato Q4 FY24 Earnings Call Transcript, p. 24
results___outcomes: The financial impact of the Tier 2 exit was visible within two quarters. Blinkit's contribution margin improved from -3.2% in Q2 FY24 to +2.1% in Q4 FY24 — the first positive contribution margin in the business's history. [Pg. 31]Blinkit achieved its first positive contribution margin of 2.1% in Q4 FY24, ahead of internal projections by approximately one quarter. — Zomato Annual Report FY24, p. 31 GOV (Gross Order Value) grew 97% YoY in Q4 FY24, reaching ₹6,832 crore, driven entirely by metro market deepening. Average order value rose to ₹612, up from ₹487. Zomato's consolidated adjusted EBITDA reached +₹194 crore in Q4 FY24, ahead of its publicly stated breakeven timeline by approximately one quarter.
sources___citations: This case study draws primarily on Zomato's publicly available financial disclosures, investor communications, and third-party industry research. All financial figures cited are in Indian Rupees (INR) unless otherwise noted. Primary sources include Zomato's Annual Report FY24, Q3 FY24 and Q4 FY24 Investor Presentations, and the Q4 FY24 Earnings Call Transcript. Secondary sources include the IBEF Quick Commerce India Report (2023), a RedSeer Consulting market sizing report on Indian q-commerce (2023), and an academic paper on last-mile logistics economics (Journal of Supply Chain Management, Vol. 59, 2023).
learning_outcomes: This case surfaces three durable strategic management principles. First, unit economics must gate geographic expansion: Blinkit's Tier 2 rollout demonstrated that GMV growth without contribution margin visibility creates compounding operational debt. Second, strategic retreat is a form of competitive aggression: by concentrating resources in metro geographies, Blinkit outspent competitors in its highest-value markets. Third, adjacent revenue streams de-risk core business pivots: the rapid scaling of Blinkit Ads provided a high-margin revenue layer that absorbed the short-term EBITDA impact of the Tier 2 exit. Students should consider: under what conditions is concentrated geographic focus preferable to wide coverage, and how should management communicate strategic retreat to public markets?
